report.source_text: The patient then underwent placement of a double-J stent with Foley catheter placement. The patient was discharged with oral antibiotics and outpatient follow-up for repeat cystoscopy and evaluation for possible stent removal in one month. The patient’s postoperative course was complicated by transient hematuria with outpatient CT urogram showing satisfactory positioning of the left ureteral stent without hydronephrosis, no contrast extravasation, and symmetric excretion of contrast material bilaterally. The patient ultimately underwent a repeat cystoscopy with left ureteroscopy and double-JJ stent removal with no noted stones, tumors within the ureter or within the renal pelvis, and no evidence of extravasation of the ureter.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old female with hypertension presented to the emergency department with acute onset severe left flank pain radiating to the left thoracic paravertebral region, associated with nausea and multiple episodes of non-bloody, non-bilious vomiting. Physical examination revealed left lower quadrant abdominal tenderness and left costovertebral angle tenderness, with normal vital signs. CT imaging of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrated an edematous left kidney with dilation of the left collecting system and moderate perinephric and periureteric fluid without an obstructing calculus. Laboratory workup showed elevated lactate (9.2 mmol/L), elevated serum creatinine (1.14 mg/dL with eGFR 53 mL/min/1.73m²), and urinalysis with moderate leukocyte esterase, 12 WBC, and 3 RBC per high-power field. Cystoscopy with retrograde pyelogram definitively confirmed the diagnosis by demonstrating contrast extravasation 2 cm distal to the left ureteropelvic junction, with no stones, filling defects, or other identifiable etiologies. The patient was treated with intravenous antibiotics and fluids, followed by double-J ureteral stent placement with Foley catheter. Postoperative course was complicated by transient hematuria. Follow-up CT urogram showed satisfactory stent positioning without hydronephrosis, no contrast extravasation, and symmetric bilateral contrast excretion. Repeat cystoscopy with left ureteroscopy and stent removal was performed without evidence of stones, tumors, or extravasation.
